title: Relational path integral, effective actions and quantum frame covariance
authors: Sergio E. Aguilar-Gutierrez, Renata Ferrero, Philipp A. Hoehn, Luca Marchetti
abstract: We propose a relational bundle-geometric formulation of the gravitational path integral by invoking the new tool of quantum reference frames (QRFs), which in gravity are gauge-covariant coordinate systems constructed from the available field content. Formulated in terms of relational (frame-dressed) observables, this yields a manifestly gauge-invariant path integral without ghosts and anomalies, and in which observables and their correlators are local to a frame. While eliminating the need for gauge fixing, it is equivalent to Faddeev-Popov versions in which the QRF is gauge-fixed, recovering certain previous proposals. A key feature is its covariance under QRF changes: it is a perspective-neutral path integral which encodes all internal QRF perspectives and the transformations between them. This leads to several qualitative predictions: local correlators and time evolution of relational observables in one QRF perspective become fuzzy in another, and a new spectrum of relational vacua arises. Comprised of frame-dependent no-boundary and asymptotic ground states, a vacuum from one perspective appears generally excited in another. Finally, we construct gauge-invariant, yet frame-dependent effective actions by coupling sources exclusively to relational observables, setting the stage for a relational definition of renormalization.
summary: This paper proposes a novel, gauge-invariant path integral formulation for quantum gravity by introducing Quantum Reference Frames (QRFs). By formulating physics using 'relational observables,' it achieves manifest gauge invariance without explicit gauge fixing. The key finding is that physical measurements become frame-dependent—localizing an event in one reference frame makes it appear 'fuzzy' when viewed from another.
main_problem: The primary goal is formulating a manifestly gauge-invariant path integral for quantum gravity that resolves issues arising from diffeomorphism invariance.
main_result: The authors propose a relational path integral formulation using Quantum Reference Frames (QRFs) which yields an anomaly-free, gauge-invariant description of gravity.
method: They develop the formalism by constructing the path integral in terms of 'relational' or frame-dressed observables, bypassing explicit gauge fixing procedures.
model_or_system: The system is Quantum Gravity, specifically addressing the gravitational path integral. The approach centers on defining physics relative to internal, dynamical reference frames (QRFs) rather than fixed background coordinates.
key_observables: Relational observables ($\hat{O}^A_R$), the relational effective action ($\Gamma_R$), and frame-change kernels ($K_{R 	o R'}$).
important_parameters: The formulation is characterized by its covariance under arbitrary QRF changes, leading to 'fuzziness' in local correlators when changing perspectives.
main_assumptions: The construction proceeds at a non-perturbative level of quantum gravity, and while gauge invariance is achieved, the relationship between dynamics across different frames requires specialized kernels.
figures_summary: Figure 1 conceptually illustrates the difference between sharply localized events in one foliation versus 'fuzzy' (field-dependent) events when viewed from another QRF perspective.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of gauge invariance in gravity, proposes the relational bundle-geometric formulation using QRFs and relational observables, derives the path integral structure, discusses the implications for vacuum states and correlators (fuzziness), and concludes by defining frame-dependent effective actions for renormalization.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum gravity, the core concept of describing physical quantities relative to internal, dynamical reference frames (QRFs) shares conceptual parallels with developing gauge-invariant descriptions in open quantum systems or time evolution when the background geometry itself is fluctuating or ill-defined.
